model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (4.8% 5yr) diverges >30% from revenue (9.4%) and EPS (29.1%). EPS is dominated by disposition gains (FY2025 includes ~$950M of gains) and is not a usable growth proxy; revenue and equity growth are aggregate figures funded by unit issuance (diluted FFO units 315M FY2023 -> 386M Q3-2026).
historical_growth.notes: The 'FCF' series for a REIT is diluted Nareit FFO per share: $6.36 FY2021, $6.03 FY2022, $6.20 FY2023, $6.14 FY2024, $6.96 FY2025 (3yr CAGR 4.9%; FY2021-25 4yr CAGR 2.3%; FY2020 not in the dataset so no 5yr). Reported FCF (OCF minus all capex) is negative every year and is not used. Per-unit FFO was flat for roughly five years to FY2024 before accelerating; FY2026 Core FFO guidance of $8.30-8.35 is ~+13% on FY2025. SBC ($80.5M FY2023 -> $93.8M FY2025 -> ~$112M FY2026E) has grown slower than FFO, so the SBC-adjusted series does not lag.

scenario_narratives.base: Backlog conversion drives two more years of high-single-digit per-unit AFFO growth, after which heavy unit issuance and debt repricing pull growth back toward the 3-5% that escalators and re-leasing spreads support. At a 9.75% cost of equity that is worth roughly 18-19x current house AFFO, well below the ~26x the market pays.
scenario_narratives.bull: A multi-year, power-constrained AI/hyperscale build-out lets DLR compound per-unit AFFO at 8-12% through FY2031 on development yields far above its cost of capital, with a lower cost of equity as the long-lease cash flows prove durable.
scenario_narratives.bear: AI capex cyclicality bites: leasing slows, the equity-funded growth flywheel reverses as the multiple compresses, recurring capex rises with density retrofits, and refinancing absorbs most organic growth -- a repeat of the flat per-unit FFO of FY2019-FY2024.

valuation_philosophy.summary: DLR is valued as a stream of per-unit AFFO to common and OP unitholders, capitalised at the cost of equity with no debt deduction. House AFFO deducts SBC, recurring capex, straight-line rent and capitalised leasing costs from Core FFO; the street basis adds SBC back. Growth is per unit on a flat count, so the dilution from the ATM programme is inside the growth path. The model says the business is excellent and the price already pays for most of the bull case: at a 5.15% risk-free rate a 3.8% house AFFO yield needs roughly 6% perpetual per-unit growth to earn a 9.75% return.
key_risks_to_valuation: AFFO bridge is rebuilt from 10-Q cash-flow lines and FY2026 guidance; capitalised leasing costs are an estimate. The Q4-2026 supplemental could move FY0 house AFFO by a few percent either way.
Cost of equity is the dominant lever: each 50bp is worth roughly 8-9% of value. A fall in the 10-year from 5.15% would lift value materially.
Per-unit growth depends on issuing equity above intrinsic value; if the multiple compresses, the same development pipeline becomes far less accretive.
Debt reprices from ~3.1% toward 5%+ over the next several years; not modelled explicitly, only through the fading growth path.
Upside risk: backlog (~$1.4-1.9bn annualised at share against ~$7.1bn revenue) could sustain double-digit per-unit growth for longer than the base path allows.
Retained AFFO (~29%) is capitalised as if distributable while also funding growth; a strict dividend-discount view would be lower.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 146.23-208.14
data_sources.financials: DLR_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt (balance sheet :2483-2509, cash flow :2761-2769, capex table :4696, FFO reconciliation :4900-4938, cover share count :2365, dividends :3989); DLR_Annual_FY2025.txt (FFO :6064, recurring capex :5771, SBC :6628); DLR_Quarterly_Q2-2026.txt for year-to-date differencing; DLR_Metrics.csv / dcf-context for history
data_sources.qualitative: DLR_Analysis.json (2026-11-15): FY2026 guidance raised 29 Oct 2026, backlog, development pipeline, ATM issuance, JV buyout and promote

inputs.sbc_source: Q3-2026 10-Q cash flow statement: amortization of share-based compensation $83.0M for nine months (DLR_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:2761), annualised to ~$112M and re-based to the current unit count ($0.30/unit x 392.6M). FY2025 actual $93.8M (DLR_Annual_FY2025.txt:6628). No separate equity-award-tax line since FY2019.
inputs.share_count_basis: 392.6M fully diluted stock + units = 378.326M common shares on the Q3-2026 10-Q cover (27 Oct 2026) + 6.649M limited-partner/incentive units (30 Sep 2026) + ~7.6M dilutive securities in the diluted FFO denominator (of which 7.17M are Teraco redeemable-NCI put shares). Held FLAT: growth is modelled per unit, with ATM / acquisition-currency dilution netted into the growth path rather than modelled as explicit unit growth (same convention as O, PSA, MAA).
inputs.fy0_basis: FY0 is FY2026 guidance (Q3-2026 release, 29 Oct 2026), not a reported year, re-based per unit. Revenue = guidance midpoint ex-promote ($7.050-7.125bn). Per-unit build: Core FFO ex-net-promote $8.325 (guide $8.30-8.35) + SBC $0.30 + non-real-estate D&A $0.11 + deferred-financing amortisation $0.09 - straight-line / above-below-market rent $0.32 - capitalised leasing compensation and internal commissions $0.17 (ESTIMATE, not in the 10-Q) = street AFFO-before-recurring-capex $8.335 (engine 'EBITDA', 46.17% of revenue on 392.6M units). Less recurring capex $1.15 (9M $242.1M + Q4 est ~$190M; Q4-2025 alone was $169M) and SBC $0.30 = house AFFO $6.885 per unit ($2,703M); street AFFO (SBC added back) $7.185 ($2,821M). The $201M Q2-2026 promote on the Blackstone JV buyout is excluded as non-recurring.
inputs.debt_memo: Real balance sheet at 30 Sep 2026 (not deducted -- AFFO is after interest and preferred dividends): total debt $19,494.6M net carrying value (revolvers $1,640.5M, term loans $424.4M, unsecured senior notes $15,809.5M, secured and other $1,620.3M); cash $802.9M (down from $3,451.6M at 31 Dec 2025); preferred stock $755.0M liquidation preference; redeemable NCI $1,596.4M. Post-balance-date: ~CHF 508M and EUR 1.0bn notes issued October 2026. Roughly 11% of debt is unhedged floating; weighted effective rate ~3.1%, so refinancing at current coupons (the October EUR notes priced at 5.125%) is a multi-year headwind to per-unit AFFO.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC -- the flow is post-interest AFFO. 10-year UST 5.15% (Yahoo ^TNX, 13 Nov 2026) + beta 0.92 x 5.0% ERP = 9.75% base. Bull 9.25% (beta 0.82: contracted long-lease cash flows), bear 10.5% (beta 1.07: AI-capex cyclicality, leverage and equity-market dependence). USD flows, USD rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Ground and operating lease costs are inside FFO already; no separate lease charge and no lease liability deducted.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flow is FFO available to common stockholders AND unitholders, already net of depreciation-adjusted NCI in consolidated entities (Teraco etc.); denominator therefore includes OP units and the Teraco put shares. Preferred dividends are deducted before FFO.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the Drivers engine with net debt held at zero (dcf-methods routing row 'REIT / property trust'). An owner-FCF DCF is meaningless here: reported FCF is structurally negative (development capex $2.6bn in nine months) and FFO/AFFO is already post-interest, so it is capitalised at the cost of equity and debt is never subtracted. Engine mapping: 'EBITDA' = street AFFO before recurring capex (Core FFO + SBC + non-RE D&A + financing amortisation - straight-line rent - capitalised leasing costs); capex path = recurring capex only; D&A and cash tax zero (REIT; foreign/TRS tax is already inside FFO); SBC deducted on the house basis. Growth paths are PER-UNIT AFFO growth on a flat unit count. CAVEATS: (1) AFFO, Core FFO and capitalised leasing costs are not in the 10-K/10-Q -- they live in the earnings 8-K ex99.1 supplemental, which is not in Extracted/; Core FFO is taken from guidance and the AFFO bridge is rebuilt from cash-flow-statement lines, with capitalised leasing costs estimated. Re-anchor on the Q4-2026 supplemental. (2) Core FFO adds back transaction/integration and other items that recur at some level (Q3-2026 Core ex-promote ~$810M vs Nareit FFO $741.5M). (3) The model capitalises full AFFO while ~29% of it is retained (dividend $4.88 vs house AFFO $6.885) and helps fund the growth in the path; this modestly flatters value, so growth paths are kept below what backlog conversion alone would suggest. (4) Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print.

bear.narrative: Hyperscaler AI capex pauses after FY2027; already-signed backlog still commences but new leasing slows, the share price de-rates so ATM issuance turns dilutive, and the 3.1% debt book reprices toward 5%+. Per-unit AFFO reverts to the FY2019-24 pattern of near-flat growth.

base.narrative: Per-unit AFFO grows 9% in FY2027 and 8% in FY2028 as the record signed-not-commenced backlog commences, then fades to 3% (escalators plus modest re-leasing spreads). Margins held flat: the per-unit mix of AFFO to revenue is assumed unchanged.

bull.narrative: Power scarcity keeps pricing power with incumbents; the 1,464 MW pipeline delivers at the ~11.6% stabilised yield, funded by equity issued at a premium multiple, so per-unit growth holds in double digits through FY2029.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 22x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear lifted to 20% and bull trimmed to 30% because DLR's growth depends on continuous external equity and debt (cash fell $2.6bn in nine months, ~$19.5bn debt at a 3.1% effective rate that reprices upward), demand is concentrated in a handful of hyperscalers whose AI capex is the cited cyclical risk, and per-unit FFO was flat for five years as recently as FY2019-24. Not higher than 20% because signed backlog and 5-15 year leases protect the in-place cash flow.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
